evidence.mechanism: shot-02s: a mirrored colony of celadon spheres under a flow gauge reading 9.0 cm/s, below the 20 cm/s tick; by shot-08s at 22.4 cm/s most of the colony has darkened to slate, but the khaki shell is barely lit.
evidence.ambition: shot-08s: one flat 2D layer of shaded spheres and thin edges plus a flow readout bar; no visible halo haze or second layer, so the ambition rests on the node state change alone.
evidence.craft: shot-02s: restrained khaki ground, clean celadon sphere shading and crisp slate label text with no artefacts; shot-08s: the dense slate nodes merge into a low-contrast murky mass in the core.
evidence.distinctness: shot-02s: coral-like branching colony on khaki with a flow gauge, unlike the apricot sand grid, dendrite type or Penrose kites of the last three nights; by shot-20s the same branch form repeats.
evidence.polish: shot-02s: colony sits centre-right against the flow gauge at left, so 2 s is composed; by shot-20s the colony has pulled back to a smaller scale with rose tips at the top, but its outline is close to shot-08s.

pairwise_justification: Tonight's branching colony with a dark core shows one clear state change from shot-02s to shot-08s; the median's Penrose kites on cream stay a static tiling with less visible development, so tonight wins the head-to-head.

critique.change: Make the khaki shell visibly lit: at shot-08s the whole colony reads slate, so raise the brightness of outer tips and keep a clear khaki rim around the dark core so the shell-versus-core split reads at a glance.
Add the boundary-layer halos already described in the brief: soft translucent khaki haze around lit branches and between tight branches at shot-08s and shot-20s, giving a second rendering layer.
Separate the murky core at shot-08s by keeping node edges legible in the dark slate state, and make shot-20s differ in outline from shot-08s by reopening branches so the core visibly thins.
